fieldData.full-article-text:
“Versions” are essentially Olympia blocks. If each version were full of transactions (which, of course, is unlikely to start), then the network’s “versions per second” rate, multiplied by the number of transactions in each version, would give you a TPS number for the Radix Public Network.

The versions/second number can be thought of as the pulse of the network that sets the length of an epoch since an epoch is a fixed number of versions in length. It’s determined by how fast the network can reach consensus – subject to latency, timeouts, etc.  One of the cool things about the 3-phase consensus we’re using for Olympia is that it can go as fast as latency, timeouts, etc., allow, rather than having a fixed duration like, say, 2-phase Tendermint. 

Further reading:

  • What’s an epoch?
  • How long is an epoch on Radix?
